title: Cast Aggregation Engine to reduce precision-switch overhead for quantized kernels
creator: Asha Patel
body:
Problem:

Our mixed-precision execution path suffers measurable per-request latency regressions when the runtime issues many small cast/dequant operations across attention heads and prefill stages. Profiling on typical conversational workloads shows a large fraction of per-token wall time consumed by short-lived kernel launches and scatter/gather casts, especially for short sequences and narrow microbatches.

Goal:

Build an in-runtime "Cast Aggregation Engine" that coalesces multiple small precision-conversion operations (INT8/FP8 <-> FP32/FP16) into fewer, larger kernels where safe to do so. The engine should be rules-driven (head/sequence aggregation thresholds) and telemetry-aware (use observed sequence length distributions and KV cache hit patterns to turn on/off aggregation). We must preserve decoding latency SLOs for 95th percentile tail while improving median and 50th token CPU/GPU utilization and reducing absolute dequant cost.

Design summary:

1) Aggregation primitives: implement a lightweight bufferization layer that can collect pending cast operations within a decode/prefill microbatch window (configurable microwindow ~1-4ms). When aggregation criteria are met (total bytes > X or num_ops > Y), emit a fused cast kernel targeting the best precision path.

2) Scope: target attention KV prefill and the decode headwise accumulation steps where current implementation performs per-head casts. Avoid aggregating across requests from different priority classes or across pinned model variants. Provide opt-out for latency-critical routes.

3) Heuristics and policy: runtime maintains rolling stats (seq_len histogram, KV cache reuse rate, microbatch occupancy). Aggregation is enabled when predicted amortized benefit exceeds a configurable threshold (latency budget saved vs. added scheduling wait). Fall back to per-op casts if queueing would breach latency SLO.

4) Kernel selection: extend kernel selector to choose either fused cast kernel or existing per-op cast kernels. Include early-cost-estimator that uses current hardware kernel throughput model (measured on device) and per-op telemetry to predict completion time.

5) Safety and correctness: fused cast kernels must be bit-true per-head when performing deterministic quantization flows; for stochastic or per-layer scale-recomputed flows we implement conservative aggregation that introduces no numerical change compared to serial ops. Add unit tests validating token-by-token parity on representative models (gpt-variants, llama variants).

6) Observability: emit fine-grained telemetry metrics: aggregated_cast_rate, avg_aggregated_bytes, aborted_aggregation_count, predicted_vs_actual_latency_delta. Surface traces in Console per-route so PMs/SEs can evaluate cost/latency trade-offs.

Acceptance criteria:

- Median token latency reduced by >= 8% on short-seq chat workload (seq <= 64) under default microbatching settings.
- 95th percentile token latency does not regress by more than 2% for any production route flagged as latency-sensitive.
- End-to-end decode correctness parity vs baseline per-op casts verified across the model suite.
- Telemetry shows aggregated_cast_rate > 25% for stable chat workloads in staging.

Rollout plan:

1) Implement engine behind a feature-flag and expose config knobs (microwindow_ms, min_bytes, min_ops, aggressiveness_level).
2) Canary rollout to non-latency routes at 10% traffic for 48 hours, monitor metrics and traces.
3) Progressive ramp (25% -> 50% -> 100%) with automated rollback on latency or error regression.

Testing and benchmarks:

- Unit tests for fused kernel correctness and scalar edge cases.
- Integration benchmarks: run the conversational benchmark suite used in runtime-performance with mixed microbatch shapes. Capture p50/p95/p99 token latency and GPU kernel occupancy.
- Cost estimate: provide break-even analysis showing token-cost delta when aggregation is enabled vs baseline for typical request mixes.

Design artifacts and links:

- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Cast+Aggregation+Engine
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8421 (WIP)
- Perf dashboards (staging): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/CastAgg/staging

Open decisions / trade-offs:

- Whether to allow aggregation across attention heads that are processed non-contiguously by kernel scheduling. Prototype uses conservative contiguous-head requirement to simplify fused kernel layout. If we can extend scheduling guarantees, we can widen aggregation scope.
- Microwindow sizing: 1-4ms seems reasonable but interacts with batching heuristics; we will experiment in canary.

Blockers:

- Need updated fused-cast kernel implementation for AMD MIG node types (scheduling differences). Blocked by low-level kernel library adaptation (ENG-44112 dependency).

Notes:

This ticket intentionally targets the runtime scheduling and kernel selection layer rather than model-level quantization policy. We expect additional gains when combined with prefix caching and adaptive microbatch sizing work (see dependencies).
